questions.solution_html:
• ExplaintheimportanceoffixationinMuseumspecimenpreparation? U/(CO5)
  • Ans: Fixation in museum specimen preparation is crucial for preserving tissue structure,
  • preventing decay, and enabling long-term display and study. It stops autolysis, kills
  • microorganisms, and hardens the specimen while maintaining a "life-like" state, allowing for
  • subsequent processing and analysis. Fixatives like formalin are used to achieve these goals.

questions.question: What precautions should be taken while storing herbarium sheets to prevent damage? / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• What precautions should be taken while storing herbarium sheets to prevent damage?
  • K/(CO5)
  • Ans: To prevent damage, the following precautions should be taken while storing
  • herbariumsheets:
  • • Keep in a Dry Environment: Moisture can cause fungal growth and decay, so store
  • sheets in a cool, dry place with low humidity.
  • • Use Insect Repellents: Place naphthalene balls or pest-repelling chemicals to protect
  • from insects like silverfish and beetles.
  • • Avoid Direct Sunlight: Store away from light to prevent fading of plant parts and
  • labels.
  • • Use Acid-Free Paper: Mount specimens on acid-free herbarium sheets to prevent
  • chemical damage over time.
  • • Label Clearly and Securely: Ensure labels are complete, typed or clearly handwritten,
  • and firmly attached.
  • • Flat, Covered Storage: Store sheets flat in closed cabinets or boxes to avoid bending,
  • dust, and physical damage.
  • • Regular Inspection: Check periodically for signs of pests, mold, or physical wear and
  • take prompt action if needed.
  • • Handle with Care: Use clean, dry hands or gloves and support sheets from beneath to
  • avoid tears or breakage.
